conceptIntro.heading: Let's build it together — Write the expression, then evaluate it in order
conceptIntro.intro: A numerical expression is a math phrase made of numbers and operations, with no equal sign. Writing one for a whole situation keeps every part visible; evaluating it means finding its single value, following the order of operations. We'll walk through a worked example, try one together, then you'll try a few with hints right there when you need them.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Evaluate in this order: grouping symbols, then powers, then multiplication and division left to right, then addition and subtraction left to right.

iDo.title: Watch me price the theater order
lines: Sofia buys 2 member tickets at $15, 4 non-member tickets at $20, and 8 student tickets at $2 each. I write one expression for each ticket type: 2 × 15, 4 × 20, and 8 × 2.
The whole order is the three costs added together: 2 × 15 + 4 × 20 + 8 × 2.
Now I evaluate. There are no grouping symbols and no powers yet, so multiplication comes first, left to right: 30 + 80 + 16.
Then I add: 30 + 80 + 16 = 126. The tickets cost $126.
linesEs: Sofía compra 2 boletos de socio a $15, 4 boletos de no socio a $20 y 8 boletos de estudiante a $2 cada uno. Escribo una expresión para cada tipo de boleto: 2 × 15, 4 × 20 y 8 × 2.
El pedido completo son los tres costos sumados: 2 × 15 + 4 × 20 + 8 × 2.
Ahora evalúo. No hay símbolos de agrupación ni potencias todavía, así que la multiplicación va primero, de izquierda a derecha: 30 + 80 + 16.
iDo.titleEs: Mírame calcular el pedido del teatro

weDo.title: Let's do one together
lines: Suppose the student tickets cost 2³ dollars each instead of $2. The expression becomes 2 × 15 + 4 × 20 + 8 × 2³.
Powers come before multiplying, so evaluate 2³ first: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8.
Then add: 30 + 80 + 64 = 174. The order now costs $174.
Sentence frame — say it with me: "My first step is ___ , because the problem asks for ___ ."
linesEs: Supongamos que los boletos de estudiante cuestan 2³ dólares cada uno en lugar de $2. La expresión se vuelve 2 × 15 + 4 × 20 + 8 × 2³.
Las potencias van antes de multiplicar, así que evalúa 2³ primero: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8.
Ahora multiplica, de izquierda a derecha: 30 + 80 + 64.
Luego suma: 30 + 80 + 64 = 174. Ahora el pedido cuesta $174.
Marco de oración — dilo conmigo: «Mi primer paso es ___ , porque el problema pide ___ .»

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake with powers is multiplying the base by the exponent: reading 3² as 3 × 2 = 6 instead of 3 × 3 = 9. A second is evaluating strictly left to right, so 3 + 4 × 2 becomes 14 instead of 11. The order of operations exists so one expression has exactly one value: grouping symbols, then powers, then × and ÷ left to right, then + and − left to right.

connect.scenario: A rideshare app charges $2.50 plus $1.75 per mile. The expression for the fare is 2.50 + 1.75m, where m is miles traveled. Your friend lives 8 miles away.
connect.promptQuestion: How much will the ride cost? How does the expression model this situation?
connect.prompt: The ride costs $___ because 2.50 + 1.75(___) = ___. The 2.50 is the ___ and 1.75 is the ___.

choices: A flat base fee charged no matter how far you go
check.explanation: 2.50 has no variable attached, so it is the constant — the flat fee you pay on any ride.
check.explanationEs: 2.50 no tiene ninguna variable pegada, así que es la constante — la cuota fija que pagas en cualquier viaje.
choicesEs: Una cuota base fija que se cobra sin importar qué tan lejos vayas

choices: The cost per mile, multiplied by the number of miles
check.explanation: 1.75 is the coefficient of m, so it is the rate: $1.75 for every mile traveled.
check.explanationEs: 1.75 es el coeficiente de m, así que es la tasa: $1.75 por cada milla recorrida.
choicesEs: El costo por milla, multiplicado por el número de millas

connect.modelAnswer: Substitute m = 8: 2.50 + 1.75(8) = 2.50 + 14 = $16.50. The 2.50 is the constant base fee charged on every ride, and the 1.75 is the coefficient — the rate charged per mile.
connect.promptEs: El viaje cuesta $___ porque 2.50 + 1.75(___) = ___. El 2.50 es la ___ y 1.75 es la ___.
connect.scenarioEs: Una app de viajes cobra $2.50 más $1.75 por milla. La expresión de la tarifa es 2.50 + 1.75m, donde m son las millas recorridas. Tu amigo vive a 8 millas.
connect.promptQuestionEs: ¿Cuánto costará el viaje? ¿Cómo modela la expresión esta situación?
connect.modelAnswerEs: Sustituye m = 8: 2.50 + 1.75(8) = 2.50 + 14 = $16.50. El 2.50 es la cuota base constante que se cobra en cada viaje, y el 1.75 es el coeficiente — la tasa que se cobra por milla.

exitTicket.stem: Quick check — you've got this: Evaluate 2 × 15 + 8 × 2³.
exitTicket.explanation: Powers first: 2³ = 8. Then multiply left to right: 2 × 15 = 30 and 8 × 8 = 64. Then add: 30 + 64 = 94.
choiceFeedback: That treats 2³ as 2 × 3 = 6, giving 30 + 48 + 46. An exponent means repeated multiplication, not multiplication by the exponent.
That adds before multiplying: (2 × 15 + 8) × 8. Multiplication comes before addition.
That leaves the power unevaluated: 30 + 8 × 15 is not the expression given.
hints: What must be evaluated before any multiplying?
2³ means 2 × 2 × 2.
After the power, multiply left to right, then add.
exitTicket.explanationEs: Primero las potencias: 2³ = 8. Luego multiplica de izquierda a derecha: 2 × 15 = 30 y 8 × 8 = 64. Luego suma: 30 + 64 = 94.
choiceFeedbackEs: Eso trata 2³ como 2 × 3 = 6, dando 30 + 48 + 46. Un exponente significa multiplicación repetida, no multiplicar por el exponente.
Eso suma antes de multiplicar: (2 × 15 + 8) × 8. La multiplicación va antes que la suma.
Eso deja la potencia sin evaluar: 30 + 8 × 15 no es la expresión dada.
hintsEs: ¿Qué se debe evaluar antes de cualquier multiplicación?
2³ significa 2 × 2 × 2.
Después de la potencia, multiplica de izquierda a derecha y luego suma.

questions.stem: In 2⁵, which number is the base and which is the exponent?
questions.explanation: The base is the number being multiplied (2) and the exponent tells how many times (5).

questions.stem: Which expression shows 5³ as repeated multiplication?
questions.explanation: The exponent 3 means the base 5 is used as a factor three times.
